Project.title: Project
Project.description: Represents an archaeological project, typically corresponding to a specific site or research initiative, which can contain multiple rock art images and their analyses.

id.description: Unique identifier for the Project entity.

name.description: The name of the archaeological project (e.g., 'Cueva de las Manos Site').

description.description: A detailed description of the project.

createdAt.description: Timestamp indicating when the project was created.

updatedAt.description: Timestamp indicating when the project was last updated.

userId.description: Reference to the unique identifier of the user who owns this project. (Relationship: User 1:N Project)

Image.title: Image
Image.description: Represents an original rock art image uploaded by the user, including its metadata and a reference to its storage location.

id.description: Unique identifier for the Image entity.

projectId.description: Reference to the Project this image belongs to. (Relationship: Project 1:N Image)

originalFileName.description: The original file name of the uploaded image.

storagePath.description: The full path to the original image file in Firebase Storage.

thumbnailStoragePath.description: Optional: The full path to a generated thumbnail image in Firebase Storage for quicker loading.

uploadTimestamp.description: Timestamp indicating when the image was uploaded to the app.

photoTimestamp.description: The date and time when the photo was originally taken, extracted from EXIF metadata.

gpsLatitude.description: The GPS latitude coordinate of where the photo was taken, extracted from EXIF metadata.

gpsLongitude.description: The GPS longitude coordinate of where the photo was taken, extracted from EXIF metadata.

gpsAltitude.description: Optional: The GPS altitude of where the photo was taken, extracted from EXIF metadata (in meters).

imageWidth.description: The width of the original image in pixels.

imageHeight.description: The height of the original image in pixels.

ImageAnalysisResult.title: ImageAnalysisResult
ImageAnalysisResult.description: Stores the details of a specific enhancement applied to an image, including the filter used, its intensity, and the path to the processed image.

id.description: Unique identifier for the ImageAnalysisResult entity.

imageId.description: Reference to the Image that was processed. (Relationship: Image 1:N ImageAnalysisResult)

filterId.description: The unique identifier of the enhancement filter applied (e.g., 'red', 'ybk').

filterName.description: The human-readable name of the enhancement filter applied (e.g., 'Rojo', 'YBK').

intensity.description: The intensity level applied for the filter, ranging from 0.5 to 3.0.

processedStoragePath.description: The full path to the processed image file in Firebase Storage.

processingTimestamp.description: Timestamp indicating when this specific image enhancement was generated.

predominantColors.description: An array of strings listing the predominant colors or pigment types detected in the processed image (e.g., ['red', 'white', 'black']). This would require an additional analysis step.

definition.description: Stores individual archaeological projects. Each project is owned by a specific user, identified by the '{userId}' in the path. This path structure enforces ownership and enables simple security rules. Includes 'userId' as the owner reference within the document.

params.name: userId
params.description: The unique identifier of the user who owns the project.

params.name: projectId
params.description: The unique identifier for the specific project.

definition.description: Stores original rock art images associated with a specific project. This subcollection requires the denormalized 'projectOwnerId' field (matching the '{userId}' path parameter) for authorization independence, allowing security rules to verify ownership without a 'get()' call to the parent project. Includes GPS and EXIF metadata.

params.name: userId
params.description: The unique identifier of the user who owns the parent project (and thus this image).

params.name: projectId
params.description: The unique identifier for the parent project.

params.name: imageId
params.description: The unique identifier for the specific image.

definition.description: Stores the results of image enhancement analyses applied to a specific image. This subcollection requires the denormalized 'projectOwnerId' field (matching the '{userId}' path parameter) for authorization independence, ensuring security rules can verify ownership without multiple 'get()' calls up the hierarchy. Includes details about the applied filter and path to processed image.

params.name: userId
params.description: The unique identifier of the user who owns the grandparent project (and thus this analysis result).

params.name: projectId
params.description: The unique identifier for the grandparent project.

params.name: imageId
params.description: The unique identifier for the parent image.

params.name: analysisResultId
params.description: The unique identifier for the specific image analysis result.

firestore.reasoning:
The Firestore structure for RupestreAI leverages a hierarchical, path-based ownership model, prioritizing Authorization Independence and secure QAPs (Query/Access Patterns). All user-specific data (Projects, Images, ImageAnalysisResults) are nested under a top-level `/users/{userId}` collection. This immediately ties every document to a specific user's authentication ID (`request.auth.uid`), making basic ownership rules simple and robust.

To ensure **Authorization Independence (CRITICAL)** and eliminate the need for `get()` calls in security rules, crucial authorization context is denormalized. Specifically, for `Image` documents and `ImageAnalysisResult` documents, the `userId` of the owning project's creator will be redundantly stored as `projectOwnerId`. This means that when a user attempts to read, create, update, or delete an `Image` or `ImageAnalysisResult`, the security rules can verify `request.auth.uid == userId` (from the path) AND `resource.data.projectOwnerId == userId` (from the document itself), without having to fetch the parent `Project` document. This allows for atomic operations and significantly simplifies rule logic, improving debuggability.

**Structural Segregation** is maintained by keeping all data within a user's `userId` path. This ensures a homogeneous security posture: all documents within a given user's branch are subject to that user's ownership rules. There are no plans for public data in this initial design, so no separate public collections are needed.

**QAPs** are inherently secure and efficient with this design. When a user requests a list of their projects (`/users/{userId}/projects`), images within a project (`/users/{userId}/projects/{projectId}/images`), or analysis results for an image (`/users/{userId}/projects/{projectId}/images/{imageId}/analysisResults`), the Firestore security rules can validate the `{userId}` wildcard against `request.auth.uid` directly, ensuring that users can only query data they own. The denormalized `projectOwnerId` further reinforces this, providing an additional layer of verification within the document.

**DBAC** is supported by directly using `request.auth.uid` for ownership. If advanced roles were needed (e.g., admin), they would be stored in dedicated collections like `/roles_admin/{uid}` for 'existence over content' checks, separate from the core data hierarchy.

**Invariants** such as ownership (`userId`, `projectOwnerId`) and timestamps (`createdAt`, `updatedAt`, `uploadTimestamp`, `processingTimestamp`) can be enforced by strict validation in the security rules during `create` and `update` operations, ensuring data integrity.
